Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
238 PM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
An area of light rain and sprinkles was developing near and east
of US-29 and will move north-northeastward through the evening.
The trend has been slightly slower and stronger for the storm
Wednesday into Thursday, but with notable lingering spread.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Coastal low pressure tonight and a cold front Monday
  delivery some rain, with cooler conditions to follow.

- 2) Rainy and breezy conditions possible over the Thanksgiving
  holiday as a coastal low tracks up the coast.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Coastal low pressure tonight and a cold front 
Monday delivery some rain, with cooler conditions to follow.

A complex and messy area of low pressure near the Southeast will
lift up off the East Coast tonight ahead of a cold front 
approaching from the Midwest. The area of low pressure had 3 
distinct centers as of mid afternoon: one east of NC, one 
offshore of SC, and one south of New Orleans. Given the strung 
out nature of the pattern, most heavier activity will remain 
east toward the immediate coast and north toward southeastern 
New England. Enough moisture and lift on the western edge of 
this broad system will continue to result in some sprinkles and 
light rain mainly east of the Blue Ridge/Catoctin Mountains 
through this evening. After midnight, the cold front approaching
from the Midwest delivers a potential for showers and sprinkles
to the Appalachians and perhaps east toward I-81. Overall 
rainfall amounts will be light and have continued to trend 
downwards. In fact, a subset of the latest model guidance has 
more rain with scattered shower activity along the cold front 
Monday than with the coastal low fringes tonight.

The cold front will cross the region Monday as low pressure
offshore moves further away. Lingering moisture and lift ahead
of an embedded shortwave may help to generate a few showers.
Otherwise, more clouds than sun is expected with northwest
breezes. Cold advection lags, so the downsloping wind may push
temperatures to near 70 in some lower elevation locations Monday
afternoon. Much cooler (and drier) air barrels in Monday night
on northwest breezes. The colder than normal temperatures linger
into the middle of the week ahead of the next storm system.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Rainy and breezy conditions possible over the 
Thanksgiving holiday as a coastal low tracks up the coast.

Behind multiple cold fronts, temperatures on Tuesday cool and return 
to late-November normals persisting throughout the week. High 
pressure builds over the Ohio River Valley giving our area a brief 
break in rainfall until Wednesday evening.

Models continue to favor an elongated trough digging into the 
Mississippi River Valley Wednesday with an associated upper- 
level low becoming cut off on Thursday. This trough sets up 
another coastal low pressure system to trail up the Mid-Atlantic
over Thanksgiving. This far out, both deterministic and 
ensemble solutions differ whether this system tracks up the east
side of the Appalachian Mountains or remains off the Mid- 
Atlantic coastline. Since last night, model trends favor a more 
western track with greater rainfall accumulation and stronger 
winds. At this time, either solution would lead to gusty winds 
and soaking rains. Depending on how fast this system can move 
into new England, precipitation diminishes overnight into Friday
morning. Breezy/gusty conditions could persist through the end 
of next week.

Across the Alleghenies, mixed wintry precipitation remains a 
possibility Thanksgiving Day, particularly at the highest 
elevations. If this were to occur, it would be brief with
marginal temperatures likely keeping any accumulating snowfall 
minimal. As the coastal low pressure pulls away, mixed wintry 
precipitation/snow showers could return to the Alleghenies and 
linger through Friday, though low-level wind direction currently
appears unfavorable for significant snow.

High pressure develops in the wake of this system bringing 
seasonable, dry conditions east of the Alleghenies Friday and 
into the start of the weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Ceilings around 2-3 kft AGL (a bit lower near CHO) will linger 
into the evening. Light rain overspreads eastern TAF sites into 
the evening. Light northerly winds are expected through tonight
generally 3-7 kts. If winds remain light and clouds break later
tonight, there may be enough lingering low-level moisture for
patchy fog. Any sub-VFR conditions should abate by early Monday
as a cold front tracks through from the west. A few sprinkles or
a brief shower could accompany the front. VFR conditions are 
expected for Monday and Tuesday with mainly northwesterly winds.
Afternoon gusts each day should peak around 20 to 25 knots, with
the strongest gusts most likely Monday evening.

Clouds increase Wednesday ahead of a coastal low pressure, but VFR 
conditions likely remain across all terminals. Gentle northwesterly 
winds shift northeasterly throughout the day and overnight. On 
Thursday, rain and sub-VFR conditions are possible with better 
chances at terminals located farther east. Northeasterly winds 
strengthen Thursday potentially gusting up to 25-35 kts.

&&

.MARINE...
Generally light winds out of the north are expected through
tonight as low pressure passes offshore. With the wavy coastal 
system being weaker in nature, any threat for Small Craft 
Advisories will occur in a limited window this evening, mainly
near southern Maryland. A cold front moves through early Monday
which favors prevailing northwesterlies which eventually turn 
more northerly by late Monday night. A secondary surge moving 
across the waters will likely require Small Craft Advisories 
Monday evening into much of Tuesday, though near SCA conditions
are possible Monday afternoon over the upper/northern waters. 
Wind gusts peak around 25 to 30 knots on Monday night into early
Tuesday morning.

Potential for gale force winds continues to be increase for the
Wed-Thu night time frame, first under E/NE flow before a low 
pressure center approaches the area, then in N to NW flow as 
the low pressure center departs the region.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A much moister environment moves into the entire region through
tonight as an area of low pressure lifts up the Carolina coast. 
Winds pick up intensity late Monday behind a strong cold front. 
This brings in cooler weather, but also another round of reduced 
daily humidities. Another coastal system may bring wet and windy 
conditions to the region Wednesday into Thursday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Relatively light winds through Monday may allow for tides to
elevate somewhat, resulting in action stages at vulnerable sites
like Annapolis, particularly late Monday afternoon. Thereafter,
strong offshore flow will result in decreasing tides Monday
night into Tuesday.

Another coastal low pressure area will likely move up the East
Coast Wednesday into Thursday. Depending on the evolution and
track, tide levels may rise once again. Current model progs vary
widely from abnormally low tides to moderate tidal flooding due
to uncertainty in exact wind direction/magnitude/low track.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$
